text: The eighth shock didn’t knock Leon over — though that wasn’t much of a victory. Even if he had wanted to, the cuffs didn’t let him fall far enough. He sagged against the filing cabinet, knees collapsed beneath him. His face was half-buried against the cabinet, forehead pressed to the cool metal, chest rising in stutters, as his breath wheezed shallow and uneven. He’d stopped trying to stand back up somewhere around pulse five. The shocks weren’t random anymore. He’d figured that out two, maybe three hits ago. It was hard to keep track now. At first, he’d thought it was just timing — bad luck, wrong place, unlucky blast. But then he’d started hearing the pattern. The shuffling footsteps. The click of dress shoes outside the door. The pause. Then the pain. It didn’t take much to figure out what was happening. He was bait. And judging by the voices in the hallway, it was working. He could hear the girls talking in the hallway outside — Meg’s boots squeaking faintly on the tile, Claudette’s voice rising and falling in concerned confusion. The worst part was how it almost made him feel safer. Leon clenched his jaw, shifting slightly as his cuffed shoulder screamed in protest. They were entirely too close. He could still hear Herman lurking somewhere not far off. The occasional hiss of static in the walls. The echo of a coat brushing tile. He swallowed hard and pressed his forehead harder to the cabinet, trying to breathe quiet. If Herman caught them too... Meg and Claudette crept along the edge of the cluster, checking each door with cautious efficiency. The Doctor’s presence stalked nearby, his heavy steps rising and falling like a tide—close enough to hear, but never consistent enough to track. The terror radius kept flaring, static thickening in the air before fading again like a faulty heartbeat. So far, he hadn’t noticed them. Didn’t mean he wasn’t waiting. Claudette gestured for Meg to hang back as they approached the corner of a side hall. Her hand hovered near the remains of what was once a rusted security gate when the air changed. Her skin prickled. The hair on her arms rose. Meg passed by, her hand within inches of connecting with the bars. “Don’t—!” Claudette yanked her back just in time. “What the hell—?!” A violent crack split the silence as static surged through the bars, leaping in arcs that sizzled and snapped like teeth. The charge danced across the frame, lashing outward with enough force to bite at Meg’s hand as she stumbled away. Her hand went instantly numb and she barely stifled a yelp, clutching her wrist. They ducked into a nearby doorway, hearts hammering as they waited for the sparking to fade. The current chased itself across nearby metal — leaping across wall rails and abandoned carts until the last crackle vanished around a corner. For a breath, everything was still. Then came the sound. A thud , dull and heavy, as something — or someone — collided repeatedly with something solid nearby. A grunt followed; muffled, but sharp enough to register pain. Meg and Claudette exchanged a wide-eyed glance. Without a word, they followed the sound. They rounded the corner just in time to see Leon’s body slam against the metal cabinet, bright sparks of electricity arcing between the nearest furniture and whatever skin they could find. His head hit first — bouncing off the surface with a sickening clunk — followed by a violent jolt down his spine as one leg kicked out involuntarily, the rest of him seizing against the cabinet’s drag. Every inch of him shuddered, teeth clenched, breath locking in his throat as his back arched off the cabinet. His cuffed shoulder twisted with the motion, muscles locking hard enough to pull his torso sideways before the shock finally relented. Claudette bolted. She dropped to her knees beside him, hands hovering in the air — uncertain where to touch without worsening the damage. Leon had slumped back again, breath ragged, muscles still twitching along one side like his body couldn’t tell if the threat had passed. His eyes were still open, but looked glazed and unfocused, as if he had completely checked out of the moment. “Hey—” Claudette’s voice broke slightly as she reached for his temple. “Leon?” She gently moved his head, brushing sweat-slick hair back to check for injury. The moment her fingers grazed his skin, his head jerked, neck going taut beneath her hands. His eyes fluttered, shaking lightly for a moment, then finally focused — or at least tried to. His gaze wandered and slid around him, until finally finding Claudette with a thin film of confusion tinted with relief. “...wh—” More of a confused breath than a question, as his misfiring system tried to piece together why he was on the floor. A bloom of pain pushed aside the haze, and he heaved a hissed stream of air through his teeth, spine curling slightly as his shoulder throbbed in protest from being yanked so low during the shock. Right. The cuff. But when did the girls get here? “God, Leon...” Claudette’s voice wavered, incredulous and breathless. “Why didn’t you say anything?” Leon blinked slowly, voice hoarse, raw around the edges. “Tried,” he rasped. “D— didn’t get far.” To one side, Meg tracked the arcs of residual static along the far wall — hissing angrily against metal debris before fizzling out. Jake hadn’t been kidding. If anything, he’d undersold it. A knot of guilt twisted in her gut as she thought of how close she’d come to sending Claudette straight into that field alone. That could’ve ended a lot worse. But the guilt burned off quickly, replaced by pure, pointed fury. “Oh, fuck this . This is absolute bullshit .” Her voice was sharp as flint. “I don’t think so.” She grabbed the chain attached to Leon’s cuff and yanked , wrapping an old rag around her hands like an impromptu insulator
